body: Unitech hit Rs 546.80 on the BSE in Jan 2008 (one of India's most valuable realty stocks), fell >90% to ~Rs 30 by Feb 2009 (one day -51% in Oct 2008), ~Rs 21.7 in 2011, ~Rs 7 by Dec 2017 (~-98.7%). Business Standard: Unitech and RCom wiped ~97% of shareholder wealth in 10 years. Visible flags: (1) 2006-07 debt-funded land purchases at cycle-peak prices; consolidated debt ballooned just as the 2008 credit crunch hit; (2) diversification into telecom (Unitech Wireless, 2008 2G licences) -- capital allocation outside the core; later CBI 2G charges against MD Sanjay Chandra (jailed 2011; brothers jailed again 2017 over homebuyer funds); (3) homebuyer advances (customer money) used to fund other projects -- ~Rs 7,800 cr owed to ~16,300 buyers across 61 projects; (4) repeated QIPs/dilution in 2009 to survive; (5) project delays and rising 'inventory' with little cash conversion. In Jan 2020 the Supreme Court allowed the government to take over the board. Lesson: in real estate, track customer-advance usage, debt/equity and land bought with borrowed money at peak; operating cash flow, not land-bank value, keeps a developer alive.

data.early_signals: debt-funded peak land buys; telecom diversification; delayed projects; customer-advance diversion; QIP dilution
data.lesson: Leverage + peak-cycle land = ruin; diversification is a red flag

title: Unitech: debt-funded land bank + 2G (2008-2020)
